label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 16
knowledgePattern: Compare ordered horizontal transformations through a functional identity
solution:
Track an original horizontal coordinate u. Applying R, then T, then S sends it through u↦−u↦4−u↦8−2u. Inverting this coordinate gives g(x)=f(4−x/2).

Applying S, then T, then R instead sends u↦2u↦2u+4↦−2u−4, so h(x)=f(−x/2−2).

Put t=−x/2−2. As x ranges over all real numbers, so does t. The identity g = h is exactly f(t+6)=f(t) for every real t. Thus C is both necessary and sufficient. It need not be the smallest period. Answer C.

hints.title: Move one point through each order
hints.body: Draw two horizontal coordinate-arrow paths starting at u, one for each transformation order. Reflection changes its sign, translation adds 4, and stretching multiplies the coordinate by 2.
hints.recap: Apply successive graph transformations in the stated order.
hints.pitfall: These are changes to point coordinates, not yet to the input written inside f.
hints.pause: Write the final coordinate for each of the two orders.

recall.reminder: Apply successive graph transformations in the stated order.

hints.title: Recover the original input
hints.body: Call each final coordinate x and solve for u. This tells you which input to f gives the transformed height at x.
hints.recap: To find a transformed function, express the old input in terms of the new coordinate.
hints.pitfall: A horizontal stretch of the point coordinate gives a division in the new function input.
hints.pause: Write g(x) and h(x), then set them equal.

recall.reminder: To find a transformed function, express the old input in terms of the new coordinate.

hints.title: Use one name for one input
hints.body: Call the input in one of those two expressions t. Rewrite the other input using t.
hints.recap: An identity must hold at every allowed input.
hints.pitfall: A repeating shift does not have to be the smallest possible period.
hints.pause: Find the difference between the two inputs and check that the resulting identity works in both directions.
